rules.instruction: Evidence-linked findings must separate observed behavior, interpretation and supported impact. Explain uncertainty where material. Do not present inferred motives, ability to pay, trust or personality as facts.

Preserve exact accepted evidence, especially negations, names, numbers, prices, dates, decision makers, attempted actions and commitments. Never translate or rewrite source quotations for the report language.

Preserve both sides of contradictory statements. Distinguish unknown, insufficient evidence and not applicable from poor performance. Unverified speaker identity and incomplete source coverage limit conclusions; a selective fact index does not establish absence.

Distinguish interaction purpose, seller role, medium and sequence. Apply expectations to the evidenced purpose: do not demand a purchase from a setter or early discovery conversation. A reference to an earlier call does not verify that call; do not invent prior discovery or later attendance.

Treat objections as statements to understand. Consider competing meanings, their evidence and a useful clarifying question. Expensive does not establish inability to pay; stakeholder consultation is not automatically an excuse. Preserve changed qualification instead of weaponizing earlier answers.

Judge discovery by useful context and solution relevance, not a fixed question count or rigid sequence. A requested brief product overview is not a premature full presentation. Credit questions and attempts already made; connect recommendations to the evidenced need.

Attribute commercial amounts and estimates to their source. Do not invent ROI, revenue loss, urgency, offer claims, commitments or a sale. Conversation quality and the commercial outcome are distinct. Preserve proposed, pending, agreed and declined states.

Use only the supplied evidence modality. A transcript cannot establish measured tone, pacing or vocal emotion; audio alone cannot establish eye contact, slide quality or visual engagement. Silence has no universal meaning. Say what cannot be determined.

Give source-grounded strengths and consequential improvements. Select one feasible next-call focus with a specific practice and source-grounded alternative phrase. Explain a possible upstream cause as interpretation. Suggested wording must not invent product facts or masquerade as a quotation.

This report covers one call. Do not claim a recurring pattern, mastery, regression, improvement over time or response to prior coaching without separately supplied longitudinal evidence. Keep this-call advice distinct from prospect facts and agreed next steps.
